latest.summary: Approving an AI service is only the starting point. As employees adopt Claude and their responsibilities change, security teams need to know who has access, which users hold administrative privileges, and whether those roles and group memberships still reflect the work they do. IBM’s 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that, among studied organizations reporting an AI-related breach, 97% lacked proper AI access controls. The finding highlights a broader challenge: AI adoption needs security practices that extend beyond the initial approval, supported by information teams can use to review access with administrators and service owners. Rapid7 Surface Command now integrates with Claude’s Compliance API, bringing supported organization, user, role, group, and settings information into the same platform teams use to understand other assets and identities. The integration helps security teams make enterprise Claude access part of their existing review practices. Bring enterprise AI access into your security view An account list tells security teams who is present, while roles and group memberships help explain how access is organized and where further review may be needed. Surface Command’s integration with Claude’s Compliance API brings together: Organizations and users: Visibility into the Claude organization and its associated user accounts. Roles and groups: Context to understand users’ assigned roles and group memberships. Organizational settings: Available configuration information to support review of the enterprise Claude environment. With those details in Surface Command, practitioners can examine Claude identities alongside the other assets and identities they manage. That gives them a clearer basis for working with service owners to evaluate whether access remains appropriate as teams and responsibilities change. The integration focuses on administrative visibility. It does not ingest Claude conversation content, provide threat detection on Claude activity, or control Claude’s behavior. From a user record to an informed access review Consider a security practitioner reviewing administrative access to Claude. In Surface Command, they can inspect an imported user’s details, review their organization role and administrative status, and examine their group memberships. The relationship graph provides a visual view of how that user connects to the organization and its groups, making those associations easier to follow. The practitioner can then work with the service owner to confirm whether administrative privileges are still needed, whether group memberships reflect current responsibilities, and whether those assignments align with the organization’s access model. Surface Command provides information to support the review, while the team applies its policies and judgment to determine whether a change is needed. Support AI adoption with clearer accountability As Claude becomes part of everyday work, reviewing its users and access relationships becomes part of managing the environment. Bringing that information into Surface Command helps security practitioners and service owners work from a shared understanding of assigned roles and group memberships. It supports more informed access decisions and helps security leaders incorporate enterprise AI into established oversight practices. Get started with Claude and Surface Command today The integration is available through the Anthropic connector in the Rapid7 Extension Library. Using Claude’s Compliance API requires a Compliance API key and the appropriate entitlement for your Claude organization. Visit the connector page to get started and see how Surface Command brings Claude users, roles, and group relationships into view.

hottest.summary: Overview On November 6, 2026, the Apache Software Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-90436 , a critical unsafe reflection vulnerability ( CWE-470 ) in Axis 1.x that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Apache Axis is a Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) implementation used for the creation of Java Web services. CISA has assigned CVE-2026-90436 a CVSS score of 9.8 Critical . Since the initial November 6 disclosure, it has transpired that some versions of Atlassian Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central use the affected Axis library and are vulnerable to CVE-2026-90436. Both products require a non-default configuration in order to be vulnerable. CVE-2026-90436 is now being actively exploited in the wild against both known affected products. On November 13, 2026, Rapid7 MDR detected exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center in a customer environment. Separately, on November 13, 2026, N-able reported exploitation in the wild against N-central for a vulnerability that strongly correlates to CVE-2026-90436. A proof-of-concept exploit that leverages CVE-2026-90436 and targets N-central was published on November 12, 2026, as part of a series of public zero-day disclosures against N-central. Rapid7 recommends remediating exposed systems on an emergency basis outside of normal patching cycles. Mitigation guidance Prioritize internet-accessible instances with the relevant APIs enabled, and check internal deployments as well. Apply the product-specific actions below, then investigate systems that were exposed for evidence of compromise. Axis 1.x through 1.4 is affected but has reached end of life (EOL) and Apache does not plan to publish a fixed Axis 1.x release. Apache recommends moving to another SOAP engine (for example, Apache Axis 2) or using an Axis 1.x build with this patch applied. Organizations using products that are affected by this issue should follow the product vendor's specific remediation instructions. Atlassian Confluence Data Center Atlassian lists versions 1.x through to 9.x as affected when “Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP)” is enabled. Version 9.2.28 is the fixed release. The setting has been off by default for new installations since version 3.0. Confluence version 10.x and later removed the feature so are not vulnerable, and Atlassian Cloud is unaffected. Affected users should upgrade to version 9.2.28 or a current unaffected 10.x release. If patching must wait, an administrator can open “General Configuration” and “Further Configuration”, edit the settings, clear “Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP)”, and save. The change takes effect without restarting Confluence, but integrations using the API may stop working. Follow the Confluence advisory for the latest fixes and mitigation instructions. N-able N-central On-premises administrators should confirm that “Legacy API” is disabled, even on 2026.4 HF2. N-able states that it is off by default, and provides instructions for disabling Legacy API . Its November 13 guidance says hosted environments received temporary protections directly; customers in both hosting models must still follow the vendor's Agent and Probe upgrade guidance. N-able also temporarily disabled the Intune integration as a precaution. Refer to the N-able security update for these responsibilities. Update: On November 16, 2026, N-able released N-central 2026.4 HF3 ( 2026.4.1.39 ) which addresses multiple issues including seventeen new CVEs. The “Legacy API” feature which exposed the vulnerable CVE-2026-90436 Axis attack surface has been disabled in this new release. N-central users should upgrade to N-central 2026.4 HF3 on an emergency basis outside of normal patching cycles. Follow the N-able advisory for the latest fixes and mitigation instructions. IOCs The presence of these IOCs in logs should prompt investigation, but the absence of these addresses does not confirm that an environment was unaffected. Atlassian Confluence Data Center The following IP addresses are associated with observed exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center: 192.238.253[.]176 5.133.47[.]243 163.182.68[.]109 104.13.106[.]166 N-able N-central N-able's November 13 incident update lists these IP addresses as IOCs for N-central customers who had not disabled Legacy API. 157.20.241[.]16 139.99.69[.]109 79.76.51[.]56 The vendor's update also lists associated URLs for use in compromise assessment. Updates November 16, 2026: Initial publication. November 17, 2026: Updated Remediation section for N-central.
